title: cli test: the #30120 start-refusal cases spawn `os start` synchronously with a 120 s spawn timeout but run under vitest's 5 s case default, so a loaded Test Core shard reds unrelated PRs
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① · Source: fleet (two unrelated PRs went red on the same shard within the hour; seat re-run records on PR #37569 and PR #37582)

## What happens

`packages/cli/test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts` (origin/main 0f6a1e518f), in the describe `#30120 — with the image switch on, a start missing its settings refuses`:
- The `refuse()` helper (:269–279) runs `spawnSync(process.execPath, [CLI, 'start', …], { timeout: 120_000 })`. That is a synchronous child `os start` with a two-minute allowance.
- The `it(...)` cases that call it (:281, :291, :298, …) pass no timeout, so they run under vitest's 5 s default.

On a loaded CI runner, one child start takes more than 5 s, and the case fails with `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` on a PR that touches nothing in `packages/cli`. The whole file took 67 s on the runner.

reach: measured twice on Test Core (5/10):
- PR #37569, run 45830682855, job 139947827254: case "only the database missing: names only OS_DATABASE_URL" (:291). The re-run went green.
- PR #37582, run 45837008571, job 139970139703: case "a switch value that is not a switch is refused too, rather than read as off" (:298).

Neither PR changes a file under `packages/cli`.

## Expected

- The `#30120` cases carry a case timeout that matches the spawn allowance (or the describe sets one), as the file's other spawning describe does with `SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS` (:325). Otherwise the case keeps a vitest timeout shorter than the work it waits on.
- No assertion changes, and no case is skipped or retried.
- Each PR that hits this today spends a re-run, and the second hit is read as a real red. This card is the place to cite.

Category ①: a named test defect that turns unrelated PRs red on a required check.
Priority: p2 — it costs every PR on that shard a re-run and makes a real red harder to see; no product behaviour is wrong.
Business reason: required CI that reds at random slows every seat's landing and trains reviewers to dismiss Test Core reds.
Reader: the lane that owns `packages/cli` tests (area:build); seat 2 closed its build intake on 11-26, so triage routes it.
Dedupe: searched `start-deployment-durability` (open issues), 0 matching cards.
Related: #30120, PR #37569, PR #37582.
